title: Why Do Shooting Stars Glow? #Shorts
description:
Why do shooting stars glow? Most are a speck of space dust about the size of a grain of sand, hitting our air so fast the air in front can't get out of the way. It gets squeezed and heats past 3,000 degrees, which boils the grain away about 60 miles up. This month's Taurids are slow and chunky, so some flare into fireballs. Best nights: around November 12.

Explained in 60 #16
